chunks: And what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man came to him and asked him about a man who married a woman and she died before he consummated the marriage with her: should he marry her mother? He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from us has done this, and we saw no harm in it.'

I said: 'May I be your ransom, the Shi'a do not boast except about the legal ruling of Ali (peace be upon him) in this 'Samjiyyah' (a specific legal case/precedent) regarding which Ibn Mas'ud gave a fatwa that there is no harm in it. Then Ali (peace be upon him) came and he asked him, and Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'From where did you take it?'
He said: 'From the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:

key_terms.اضطراب الإسناد: Instability or weakness in the chain of narrators.
key_terms.سَمْجِيَّةٌ: A specific legal precedent or case, often referring to a ruling by Ibn Mas'ud regarding marriage.
key_terms.قَضَاءُ عَلِيٍّ: The legal ruling or verdict attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib.
key_terms.لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ: No blame or sin upon you (Quranic phrase indicating permissibility).
key_terms.مُرْسَلَةٌ: General or unrestricted (referring to a Quranic verse that is not an exception).
key_terms.مُسْتَثْنَاةٌ: Excluded (referring to a Quranic verse that is an exception to a general rule).

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry the mother of a deceased wife if the marriage was not consummated?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia methodological principle of *al-waqf* (suspending action) when a hadith appears to contradict the apparent meaning (*zahir*) of the Quran, specifically regarding the marriageability of a deceased wife's mother. It contrasts Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) practical allowance of the practice with Ali ibn Abi Talib’s (AS) critical analysis of the Quranic verse (4:23), distinguishing between the general prohibition and specific exceptions. The text concludes that due to this apparent discrepancy and the weak (*shadh*) nature of the chain, these reports are not sufficient for independent legal derivation without reconciling them with stronger evidence.
